references.text: Isaiah invites all who thirst to come and drink – God offers spiritual satisfaction without cost. This stands in contrast to the earthly water Jesus speaks of, which only gives temporary satisfaction. See [ref:Jes 55:1-2|Isaiah 55:1-2].

The next verse expands on this contrast: while whoever drinks from the well will thirst again, whoever drinks from the water Jesus gives will never thirst again. [ref:Joh 4:14|John 4:14] is the direct continuation and resolution of the statement in verse 13.

Jesus uses a similar image when he calls himself the bread of life: whoever comes to him shall not hunger, and whoever believes in him shall never thirst. The theme that earthly food cannot satisfy forever, while Jesus gives lasting satisfaction, is the same. See [ref:Joh 6:35|John 6:35].

Jesus contrasts the heavenly bread with the manna the fathers ate in the wilderness – those who ate the manna still died. The parallel is clear: earthly food and drink give only temporary satisfaction, while what Jesus gives lasts forever. See [ref:Joh 6:58|John 6:58].

During the Feast of Tabernacles, Jesus cries out that whoever thirsts should come to him and drink, and streams of living water will flow from within the believer. Only Jesus can give water that truly quenches thirst forever. See [ref:Joh 7:37-38|John 7:37-38].

In the new creation, God promises to let the thirsty drink freely from the spring of the water of life – the final fulfillment of the promise of water that quenches all thirst, in contrast to earthly water which only gives temporary relief. See [ref:Åp 21:6|Revelation 21:6].

The Israelites thirsted in the wilderness and received water from the rock at Horeb – but they thirsted again later. This historical example illustrates the point that physical water only temporarily satisfies thirst. See [ref:2 Mos 17:3-6|Exodus 17:3-6].

The Lord accuses his people of having forsaken him, the fountain of living water, and instead hewn out cisterns that cannot hold water. The contrast between broken cisterns and the fountain of living water highlights the same theme Jesus draws upon. See [ref:Jer 2:13|Jeremiah 2:13].
